meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'or', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('bad').

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Common feminine noun meaning 'mistake, error' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are many serious mistakes in the case.

examples.text: А прокуратура думает иначе. В деле много грубых ошибок.
examples.trans: The prosecutor's office thinks otherwise. There are many serious mistakes in the case.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my own', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'labour, work' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The job centre is over there.

examples.text: А ты иди на биржу труда. Там есть работа.
examples.trans: You go to the job centre. There's work there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'знавать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to admit, to recognise', paired with 'признать'.

examples.text: То есть вы признаёте свою ошибку?
То есть вы признаёте, что брали взятки?
examples.trans: So you admit that you took bribes?

examples.text: Там сидит критик, умей спокойно признавать ошибки.
examples.trans: A critic is sitting there, learn to calmly admit mistakes.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to give; (imperative) let's', paired with 'дать'.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

тереть.gloss: to rub, to scrub, to grate

meanings.en: to rub, to scrub, to grate
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to rub, to scrub, to grate', paired with 'потереть'.

examples.trans: He tiredly rubbed his eyes with his hands.

examples.text: Аркашка, ты еле стираешь! Сильнее три!
examples.trans: Arkashka, you're barely washing! Rub harder!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'truth; honestly' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'oneself, myself, himself', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

examples.text: Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'бирать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to choose, select, pick'.

examples.trans: He takes a long time choosing a new dish.

examples.text: Выбирай слова, когда говоришь с ней!
examples.trans: Choose your words when talking with her!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to live'.

examples.trans: I live in a communal flat.

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'whether, if; (что ли) or what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I don't know whether he is at home.
Was it Osipenko who hired you?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'peace; world' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'illusion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Мы очень часто существуем в иллюзиях.
examples.trans: We very often exist in illusions.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть иллюзия.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always illusion.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'leave, abandon'.

examples.text: Вика, ну он одинокий. Я же не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: Vika, come on, he's all alone. I can't just leave him on his own.

examples.text: Я же не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: I can't just leave him on his own.

examples.text: Ты что, голову в Москве оставил?
examples.trans: What, did you leave your head in Moscow?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'шлый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('last, past, previous').

examples.text: В прошлый раз я думала, война началась.
examples.trans: Last time I thought a war had started.

examples.text: Марина, ну опять ты со своей сгущёнкой! В прошлый раз я думала, война началась.
examples.trans: Marina, there you go again with your condensed milk! Last time I thought a war had started.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to move', paired with 'двинуться'.

examples.text: Никому не двигаться с этого места!
Главное — помнить свои уроки и двигаться вперёд.
examples.trans: The main thing is to remember one's lessons and move forward.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'forward, ahead', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы взяточник! Вы лезете вперёд больного ребёнка.
examples.trans: You're a bribe-taker! You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.
You're pushing in ahead of a sick child.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'sometimes, at times', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Иногда наши победы бывают слишком странными.
examples.trans: Sometimes our victories turn out too strange.
Sometimes it is useful to trust others.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'choice' in everyday Russian.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'very, very much', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pizza' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free.

examples.text: Анатолий Иванович, тут доставка пиццы. Пишут, доставим за десять минут.
examples.trans: Anatoly Ivanovich, there's pizza delivery here. They write: we'll deliver in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to order', paired with 'заказывать'.

examples.text: Если опоздают, пицца бесплатно. Может, закажем?
examples.trans: If they're late, the pizza is free. Maybe we should order?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'конец-то'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

заходить.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.en: to come in, to drop in
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to come in, to drop in', paired with 'зайти'.
High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hi', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thing' in everyday Russian.
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'винить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to excuse; (imperative) sorry, excuse me', paired with 'извинять'.

examples.trans: Thank you, Marina. Sorry, I'm in a hurry.
